correctness.rationale: The quadratic-difference tournament has exactly 42 directed cyclic triples and no cell dimension≥2 by unique pair common-neighbor intersections. My independently written finite enumeration gives 42 Hom vertices, 63 coordinate-toggle edges, a connected cubic graph with a complete 41-edge spanning tree and free threefold coordinate-rotation quotient of 14 vertices and 21 edges. Explicit orbit adjacency matches the Fano (7,3,1) cyclic difference system, hence Heawood graph and a connected regular covering. Collapsing a spanning tree gives H1=Z^22; rational transfer gives eight invariant cycles (Heawood beta1=8), so remaining 14 dimensions are seven copies Q(zeta3) with nonidentity trace +1. This is a finite complete graph argument, not an infinite Paley theorem.
